      October 23, 2026

                    ICYMI: Transformational Jobs, Investment Continue Across Georgia

ATLANTA - 
In case you missed it, Governor Brian Kemp and the Georgia Department of Economic Development under the leadership of Commissioner Pat Wilson have announced transformational job and economic growth across all four corners of Georgia throughout the late summer and early fall. Building on another 
record-breaking year
 for investments from state-worked economic development projects in FY2026, announcements have continued to be made that companies are choosing Georgia for expansions and new locations that will offer opportunities for meaningful careers for hardworking Georgians.
Below, please see a full recap of economic announcements from recent months, with more to come in the days ahead.
Mitsubishi Power Doubles Footprint in Chatham County
October 23, 2026
Governor Brian P. Kemp today announced that Mitsubishi Power Americas, Inc. (Mitsubishi Power) is investing $490 million in expanding its existing footprint in Georgia. The company plans to create more than 220 new jobs in Chatham County.
“When we met with Mitsubishi Power and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries in Tokyo, we came away with a deeper understanding of how the company could continue growing in Georgia. We are excited that the Savannah Machinery Works is expanding to turn those possibilities into reality,” 
said Governor Brian Kemp
. “
Congratulations
 to all those who worked hard to support this job creator and the opportunities they will bring Georgians for over a decade, building on their long history as a valued member of this community.”
Mitsubishi Power is a power solutions brand of Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Ltd. (MHI). Mitsubishi Power’s power generation solutions include gas, steam, and aero-derivative turbines; power trains and power islands; geothermal systems; environmental controls; and services. It also offers solutions that leverage AI-enabled autonomous operation of power plants. Headquartered in Tokyo, Japan, MHI is one of the world's leading heavy machinery manufacturers with engineering and manufacturing businesses spanning energy, infrastructure, transport, aerospace, and defense.
***
Full release: 
https://gov.georgia.gov/press-releases/2026-10-23/gov-kemp-mitsubishi-power-doubles-footprint-chatham-county
Blue Bird Invests $300 Million in Peach County
October 21, 2026
Governor Brian P. Kemp today announced that Blue Bird Corporation (Blue Bird), a technology leader and innovator of school buses, is expanding its existing footprint in Peach County. The company plans to invest an estimated $300 million in a new manufacturing facility in Fort Valley, creating 375 new jobs over the next three years.
“For nearly 100 years, Blue Bird has been an incredible part of Georgia’s story, and now that story will continue to be written for years to come,” 
said Governor Brian Kemp
. “We are proud when our long-time partners can grow and adapt to changing markets right here in the Peach State, and this expansion is the latest example that our pro-business environment is fostering sustained success for our business partners. I want to congratulate Blue Bird, Fort Valley, and Peach County on this announcement and their continued prosperity.”
Blue Bird school buses are available in a wide range of options and configurations to meet the diverse needs of school districts worldwide. The company has set industry standards through innovative design, engineering excellence, and advanced manufacturing capabilities, and currently supports more than 1,900 employees in Georgia.
***
Full release: 
https://gov.georgia.gov/press-releases/2026-10-21/gov-kemp-blue-bird-invests-300-million-peach-county
VDL Groep Adds 120 New Jobs in Hall County
October 13, 2026
Governor Brian P. Kemp today announced that VDL Groep (VDL), a global Dutch mechanical engineering and equipment manufacturer, will invest an estimated $77 million over the next several years to expand its footprint in Hall County, creating approximately 120 new jobs.
“Companies like VDL Groep not only continue to choose Georgia for an initial investment, they also choose to grow their footprint here again and again because of our pro-business environment and partnership approach,” 
said Governor Brian P. Kemp
. “That includes our efforts to be the Top State for Talent, so manufacturers like VDL Groep have the reliable, highly-skilled workforce they need to succeed.”
VDL Industries Gainesville, part of Netherlands-based VDL Groep, is a turnkey partner in the development and manufacturing of high-tech systems. The unique combination of technical expertise and high-quality craftsmanship under one roof enables VDL to provide integral solutions in the high-tech semiconductor, foodtech, mobility, and infratech sectors. Currently employing approximately 70 people in Hall County, VDL has already strengthened its position in sheet metal fabrication, welding, machining, and cleanroom system integration.
***
Full release: 
https://gov.georgia.gov/press-releases/2026-10-13/gov-kemp-vdl-groep-adds-120-new-jobs-hall-county
Hyundai Transys Bringing 320 New Jobs to West Point
October 8, 2026
Governor Brian P. Kemp today announced that Hyundai Transys will invest nearly $560 million to expand its manufacturing capabilities in West Point, Georgia. The company plans to create 320 new jobs as part of its ongoing efforts to support global automotive customers with operations in North America.
“The Hyundai family of brands has been an incredible partner to Georgia, and this decision by Hyundai Transys only reinforces that valued friendship,” 
said Governor Brian P. Kemp
. “As the automotive manufacturing industry continues to make historic investments in our state, this facility will further enhance the strength of that ecosystem and allow Hyundai and Kia to grow their already impressive capacity here in Georgia.”
Since its founding in 1994, Hyundai Transys has grown into a global automotive parts specialist, focused on advanced technology and quality powertrains and seats. The company currently supports roughly 1,250 jobs at its West Point facility.
***
Full release: 
https://gov.georgia.gov/press-releases/2026-10-08/gov-kemp-hyundai-transys-bringing-320-new-jobs-west-point
MEC Plans Approximately 140 New Jobs in Thomson
October 1, 2026
Governor Brian P. Kemp today announced that Mayville Engineering Company (MEC) plans to create approximately 140 new jobs and invest an estimated $26 million over the next several years to establish a new metal fabrication facility in McDuffie County.
“We continue to see companies bring good-paying jobs and opportunity to all corners of this state,” 
said Governor Brian P. Kemp
. “MEC will help reinforce Georgia's strong manufacturing supply chain while benefiting from our highly skilled workforce and top-notch infrastructure network.”
Founded in 1945, MEC is a U.S.-based company that provides a wide range of services, including prototyping and tooling, production fabrication, aluminum extrusion, coating, assembly, and aftermarket support. The company serves various industries, such as commercial vehicles, data center and critical power, construction and access equipment, agriculture, powersports, and more.
***
Full release: 
https://gov.georgia.gov/press-releases/2026-10-01/gov-kemp-mec-plans-approximately-140-new-jobs-thomson
Pirelli to Invest $1.2 Billion in Georgia Expansion
September 22, 2026
Governor Brian P. Kemp today announced that Pirelli, a world leader in tire production, will create 1,000 new jobs as part of a multi-year, $1.2 billion expansion of its existing facility in Rome, Georgia. Governor and First Lady Kemp previously met with Pirelli's executives while leading an economic mission to Italy in 2024, laying the groundwork for this announcement.
“For over two decades, Pirelli has been a valued presence in our state, and I'm thankful that our efforts to grow this partnership are paying off with even more jobs for hardworking Georgians,” 
said Governor Brian P. Kemp
. “This historic investment will expand Pirelli's footprint with roughly five times more positions than they currently employ across the region, and we wish them continued success here in the No. 1 state for business."
Headquartered in Italy, Pirelli located its U.S. headquarters and manufacturing facility in Rome, Georgia, in 2002. Pirelli currently employs 234 Georgians through its manufacturing, innovation, and headquarters operations in the state.
***
Full release: 
https://gov.georgia.gov/press-releases/2026-09-22/gov-kemp-pirelli-invest-12-billion-georgia-expansion
Walmart to Bring 1,000 Jobs, Next-Gen Fulfillment Center to Carnesville
August 27, 2026
Governor Brian P. Kemp today, while continuing an economic development mission in South America, announced that Walmart, Inc. plans to build a high-tech, next-generation fulfillment center in Carnesville, creating 1,000 new jobs and bringing $1.3 billion in investment to Franklin County.
“This massive investment from Walmart in a rural part of our state will not only create new, good-paying jobs for hardworking Georgians, it will also allow them to work close to home rather than commuting to a larger city for work,” 
said Governor Brian P. Kemp
. “Every Georgian should have opportunity, no matter their zipcode, and Walmart is helping us deliver on that promise.”
Walmart’s presence in Georgia includes 209 Walmart stores and Sam’s Clubs, as well as 11 supply chain facilities, employing more than 65,300 associates across the state. The retailer also supports local businesses in Georgia, spending more than $26.2 billion with Georgia suppliers and supporting more than 167,600 supplier jobs in fiscal year 2025, alone.
***
Full release: 
https://gov.georgia.gov/press-releases/2026-08-27/gov-kemp-walmart-bring-1000-jobs-next-gen-fulfillment-center-carnesville
Cirkla to Bring 140 New Jobs to Hall County
August 17, 2026
Governor Brian P. Kemp today announced that Cirkla will invest more than $5 million to establish a new food packaging manufacturing facility in Gainesville, Georgia. The project is expected to create approximately 140 new jobs in Hall County over the next three years.
“Cirkla's choice to build their packaging solutions facility in the heart of one of Georgia's strongest export hubs is a testament to our state's logistics capabilities and assets,” 
said Governor Brian P. Kemp
. “Investments in infrastructure by the Georgia Ports Authority, including the brand-new Gainesville Inland Port, are helping deliver products to markets all over the world, and we look forward to Cirkla's success as a result.”
Cirkla, a global leader in developing and manufacturing molded fiber solutions, helps brands meet their packaging sustainability goals through expertise spanning material science, product design and development, mold design, laminations, and coatings.
***
Full release: 
https://gov.georgia.gov/press-releases/2026-08-17/gov-kemp-cirkla-bring-140-new-jobs-hall-county
DeltaX to Establish North American HQ in Walton County
August 14, 2026
Governor Brian P. Kemp today announced that DeltaX, a global provider of advanced battery energy storage solutions (BESS), will create approximately 250 new jobs and invest $141 million to establish its North American manufacturing headquarters in Walton County.
“The decision by DeltaX to locate its headquarters here and further grow Georgia's energy sector is another testament to our position at the forefront of innovation and emerging technology,” 
said Governor Brian P. Kemp
. “Projects like this are possible because of our cutting-edge research universities, world-class workforce training, and reliable energy infrastructure, and I look forward to the opportunities it will bring to the people of Walton County."
Headquartered in Seoul, South Korea, DeltaX develops advanced Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), intelligent Battery Management Systems (BMS), and AI-powered energy management technologies. The company provides integrated energy storage solutions for utility-scale projects, renewable energy integration, AI data centers, commercial and industrial applications, and OEM customers worldwide. Through proprietary battery engineering, thermal management, embedded software, and artificial intelligence, DeltaX delivers high-performance, safe, and reliable energy storage platforms for the global energy transition.
***
Full Release: 
https://gov.georgia.gov/press-releases/2026-08-14/gov-kemp-deltax-establish-north-american-hq-walton-county
Siemens Plans 1,400+ New Jobs in Jackson County
August 7, 2026
Governor Brian P. Kemp today announced that Siemens is planning to create more than 1,400 jobs at its new advanced manufacturing facility in Pendergrass over the next three years. The project represents at least $185 million in investment in Jackson County, pending final approvals.
“For 140 years, Siemens has been a valued part of Georgia’s business community, and this latest investment decision is another testament to the strong economic partnership between our state and Germany,” 
said Governor Brian P. Kemp
. “We are proud to support this next chapter of growth and look forward to the impact of these quality jobs on the Pendergrass community and the surrounding area.”
Siemens is a global technology company and a leader in electrification, automation, and industrial software. Siemens currently supports over 1,700 employees across two manufacturing facilities and six offices in the state, including Siemens’ Peachtree Corners Electrical Products facility.
***
Full release: 
https://gov.georgia.gov/press-releases/2026-08-07/gov-kemp-siemens-plans-1400-new-jobs-jackson-county
Highline Warren Plans Multi-Year, $170M Investment in Henry County
July 14, 2026
Governor Brian P. Kemp today announced that Highline Warren, an American vertically integrated distributor of automotive aftermarket and cleaning products, is investing $170 million in a new logistics and operations center in McDonough. The multi-year investment will create 160 new jobs.
“Like so many other businesses, Highline Warren recognizes Georgia’s advantages when it comes to affordably producing and efficiently moving products to market,” 
said Governor Brian Kemp
. “With reliable logistics infrastructure that includes the fastest growing port on the East Coast, our state offers unmatched connectivity and a highly-skilled workforce that leads to success. This investment will further grow opportunities for hardworking Georgians, and I want to thank Highline Warren for choosing us.”
Headquartered in the United States, Highline Warren distributes and manufactures maintenance and cleaning solutions for automotive, home, commercial, and industrial applications. Through a network of facilities spanning the country, the company produces, sources, and delivers over 30,000 consumable products, including automotive fluids, chemicals, filters, and cleaning solutions. The company currently employs an estimated 1,700 teammates and serves thousands of customers across North America.
***
Full release: 
https://gov.georgia.gov/press-releases/2026-07-14/gov-kemp-highline-warren-plans-multi-year-170m-investment-henry-county
